transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes (recording)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood Partnerships), Jared (CrystalGrid), Aisha (CG VP Sales), Marco (CG Solutions Arch), Priya (CG Security)

Summary (auto):
Partner intro and discovery between CrystalGrid (GPU/cloud vendor) and Redwood Inference. High-level go-to-market alignment, technical capabilities (H100/A100 support, private VPC/on-prem options), initial integration surfaces (marketplace listing, private deployment automation), and next steps for benchmarks and technical deep dive.

Topics:
- CrystalGrid product + fleet (H100 nodes, bare metal, zone availability)
- Redwood Dedicated/Private deployment model and integration requirements
- Security/compliance (KMS, SOC2, audit logs, SSO)
- Pilot/benchmark plan and commercial outlines

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have a bunch on the agenda - quick intros then we'll go through high level partnership goals.
[00:18] Jared: Yep thanks Maya, Jared from CrystalGrid, uh we run a GPU cloud and partner program, excited to learn how Redwood runs inference across hosted and private.
[00:28] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here, want to understand co-sell and commercials - what does success look like for a partner like us.
[00:35] Samir: Hey all, Samir from Redwood SE - I'll focus on the tech; quick note we typically support H100 and A100, multi-tenant hosted, and Private (VPC) installs with a control plane we can co-manage.
[00:48] Marco: Sounds good, two quick things from me - one, network/topology for private deploys; two, how does the KV cache and prefix caching interact with shared clusters, we see odd cache invalidation patterns sometimes - or, or sorry kay vee cache i think that's how my team says it.
[01:05] Samir: Yeah, kay vee cache, classic; so Redwood runtime manages KV cache per model session and we have options - isolated caches for customer tenants on Dedicated pools, or namespace-scoped caches on shared capacity. That affects memory footprint and cold-start behavior.
[01:24] Priya: From security: we need to see KMS integration, key lifecycle, audit logs, and SSO (SAML). Do you have SOC 2 Type II?
[01:34] Maya: We do, yes - Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have KMS integrations with common cloud KMS and HSM options for Private. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:44] Jared: Great. On the product side, we run dedicated bare-metal H100 instances and want to offer a managed Redwood runtime as a marketplace add-on or preinstalled image. Curious how the control plane talking looks for Private - do you need outbound to our control plane or can it be air-gapped?
[02:02] Samir: We support both. For VPC deployments we usually have a private control plane with limited outbound for telemetry; for air-gapped/on-prem we provide an offline installer and a customer-managed control plane. The typical pattern is two modes: co-managed control plane (TLS to Redwood endpoints) or fully customer-managed with audit log shipping.
[02:22] Marco: Ok ping, that helps. What about model versions and rollouts? We want to ensure we can pin models to certain GPU SKUs or limit tenancy when customers request SLAs.
[02:33] Samir: We have rollouts and pinning - you can route requests by model version or by policy (latency or cost). You can also create node pools tagged by SKU (e.g. h100-2026-32gb) and pin traffic. Fallbacks can route to compatible quantized variants.
[02:51] Aisha: From a go-to-market lens, what are other partners typically looking for? Marketplace placement, joint case studies?
[02:58] Elena: We usually aim for listing in our partner catalog, co-marketing for joint customers, and a pilot to validate perf/cost. Case study once we hit production.
[03:08] Jared: Pricing question - how do you think about unit economics, e.g. per-token cost vs latency? If our customers care about low latency for real-time apps, they'll pick dedicated low-latency nodes but cost increases.
[03:22] Maya: Exactly, it's a tradeoff; Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to cut token cost while keeping latency SLOs. For co-sell materials we'll include typical unit economics and reference workloads.
[03:34] Marco: Can you run benchmarks on our infra to show perf? We often see vendors overclaim.
[03:40] Samir: Yes, we'll run a 48h benchmark using your H100 cluster - we'll need network diagrams, expected concurrent request patterns, typical sequence lengths. I'll share a template.
[03:52] Jared: Good. Also, we need an integration story for our managed control plane customers vs bare-metal customers.
[03:59] Maya: For managed customers we can offer a hosted Redwood API fronting the runtime, or onboard Redwood Dedicated tied to a customer-specific pool on your infra. For bare-metal we offer images and Helm charts for the runtime.
[04:12] Priya: On the security side, if we offer a prebuilt image, we need to run SBOM scanning and know what dependencies are included. Also, what about encrypted logs and retention policies?
[04:24] Samir: We produce SBOMs for official release images and support encrypted audit logs to your S3 or event stream. Retention policies are configurable, and we can redact tokens on ingest if needed.
[04:37] Jared: Curious on operational footprint - what GPU counts do you recommend for pilot vs production?
[04:44] Samir: Pilot: 4-8 H100s to validate latency/throughput; production depends on concurrency and sequence length - typical LLM text-generation workloads often need 32+ GPUs across zones for high availability. But we can start small.
[05:00] Aisha: Commercial model - do you license a runtime or do you charge usage?
[05:06] Maya: We have a few models: usage-based for hosted API, reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated (commit + monthly), and enterprise licensing for Private deployments. For marketplace partners we often do revenue share or a reseller arrangement.
[05:17] Elena: And for channel partners we can do joint pipeline credits to seed trials.
[05:21] Marco: Technical detail - how do you handle continuous batching? If we route traffic through a shared ingress, can batching cross-tenant requests? We need isolation.
[05:32] Samir: Batching never mixes tenant contexts for safety; we batch within logical partitions. We also have latency-aware batching so small requests don't get held too long.
[05:45] Jared: Ok good. A few questions from my engineering team (I've got them typed here): network egress, port requirements, and whether Redwood uses gRPC or REST for runtime communication.
[05:54] Samir: Runtime supports both HTTP/REST and gRPC. For private deployments we prefer gRPC for perf. Ports listed in the integration doc - we'll share the exact port matrix. Egress is minimized and we can provide an allowlist for endpoint calls.
[06:08] Maya: Cool, sounds like we have alignment on the big pieces. Marco, anything specific you want us to measure in the benchmark?
[06:14] Marco: Yes, measure 95th and 99th latency for 512-token sequences at 5 and 20 concurrent requests, throughput (tokens/s), GPU memory utilisation, and cold vs warm start latency. Also include quantized model runs (4-bit) to compare cost/loss.
[06:30] Samir: Got it. We'll include quantized variants.
[06:34] Priya: Please include data residency notes - some customers in Europe will insist data never leaves EU.
[06:41] Maya: We can pin deployments by region and provide data residency controls, yes.
[06:46] Jared: Next, support model onboarding - do you help customers bring custom models or only pre-curated ones?
[06:52] Samir: We support both. We onboard common open models and have a model onboarding process for customer models - we do compatibility checks, quantization recommendation, and perf tuning.
[07:03] Aisha: For GTM, how long until we can go to market? Assuming we do a pilot in July, what's realistic?
[07:10] Maya: Typical pilot is 4-8 weeks including benchmarks and integration; if everything looks good, joint go-to-market assets and marketplace listing can follow after a successful pilot, so 8-12 weeks to public launch in a fast flow.
[07:21] Marco: A note on storage - some customers use large embedding stores; does Redwood recommend a vector DB or built-in caching?
[07:29] Samir: We integrate with several vector DBs but also have a local KV cache for prefixes; for large-scale embedding workloads we recommend an external vector store and provide connectors.
[07:40] Jared: Any blockers you see from your side to run a benchmark on our infra?
[07:45] Samir: We'll need access (read-only/agent) to a staging cluster or a list of endpoints, a network runbook, and a contact for onboarding - Marco volunteered earlier. Also API keys for any internal test harness.
[07:59] Marco: I'll gather that and share.
[08:03] Maya: Great. A few quick product clarifications - Redwood Optimize suggestions can be exported as policy templates for autoscaling and batching; Redwood Console provides per-route latency/cost breakdowns - helpful when we debate routing to cheaper GPUs.
[08:19] Aisha: Can we co-brand the console for marketplace customers?
[08:23] Elena: We have white-label options for enterprise partners, usually behind a partner agreement. We'll include that in the partner packet.
[08:31] Jared: On the commercial front, if we do a reseller model, how do margins get handled and who manages support?
[08:38] Maya: Typically partners resell Dedicated/Private with a margin and Redwood handles product support while partners handle first-line commercial support; we can tailor the split.
[08:48] Marco: Security follow-up: Priya will need a SOC2 artifact and a list of sub processors.
[08:53] Maya: We'll send SOC2 and sub-processor list in the security pack.
[08:58] (short silence / crosstalk checking mics)
[09:05] Samir: One implementation note - for air-gapped installs we have an offline bundle but there's some manual steps for KMS/HSM integration, and key-wrapping calls may be required. We'll document those.
[09:18] Jared: Perfect. Anything else on the technical side?
[09:22] Marco: Not from me, I'll make sure to follow up with topology and a list of test clusters.
[09:27] Aisha: From sales I'll want a one-pager with commercial motions and some reference metrics to show to prospects.
[09:33] Maya: We'll do that and include typical unit economics examples.
[09:37] Elena: We'll also propose a joint pilot package with credits to seed a couple customers.
[09:42] Jared: Sounds good - again we want the ability to preinstall Redwood runtime on our marketplace images. How are updates handled?
[09:49] Samir: We can push updates via image refresh for marketplace images; for customer-managed runtimes we provide upgrade manifests and an optional managed upgrade path.
[09:59] Priya: For compliance, do you support provisioning audit logs to external SIEMs?
[10:06] Samir: Yes we support external log push to SIEMs and have hooks for alerting.
[10:13] Maya: Ok, I'll do a quick recap and next steps.
[10:16] Maya: Recap — Redwood to send partner packet (security docs, SOC2, partner playbook), Samir to send benchmark template and port matrix, Marco to share network diagram and test cluster details, Maya to draft commercial outline and propose pilot credits. We agreed on a 4-8 week pilot, measure 95/99 latencies and throughput, and include quantized runs.
[10:37] Jared: That matches our notes. Any proposed dates?
[10:40] Maya: We'll aim to start the benchmark week of 2026-07-20, Samir can kick it off once Marco provides access.
[10:47] Marco: Sounds good.
[10:49] Aisha: I'll sync internally and provide a list of target customers we want to seed.
[10:53] Maya: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the email and attachments.
[10:58] (meeting closes)
